title: A loop stalled on sign-in tells the person again when they come back to the Mac
goal: When the loop cannot sign in it says so once, at the moment it stalls, and then once a day. On 2026-09-30 that one notice went out at 10pm, nobody was at the Mac, and the loop sat idle for about twenty hours until the person happened to sign in again the next evening. It should also tell them the first time they come back to the Mac while it is still stalled.
notes: Evidence: queue/loop.log shows sign-in failures from 2026-09-30 22:05 to 2026-10-01 18:25 local (39 attempts); queue/history.jsonl has a single stall_notified event at 2026-10-01T05:05:09Z (hours 0). notify_person and the once-a-day rule are in queue/bin/go-loop.sh; person-at-mac.sh reads HIDIdleTime. loop-day.mjs for that day: tasks 10.8 per cent, between 74.9 per cent.
acceptance: While the loop is stalled on sign-in or the spend limit, the first time the person returns to the Mac after being away (the same idle reading the walks use) they get one notice naming the action that ends the stall
At most one such notice per return, and none once the stall has cleared
A drill shows it: a stalled loop, the person away then back, exactly one notice; the person back with no stall, none
The dashboard and loop.log say when the return notice went out

log.note: owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Reproduced from the record: queue/history.jsonl has one stall_notified (2026-10-01T05:05:09Z, hours 0) for a sign-in stall that loop.log shows lasting to 18:25 the next day; nothing between. Built: advancePresence in queue-lib.mjs (away after PHOTONZ_STALL_AWAY=900s of no input, a return is the next reading with input, one notice per return, presence fields survive retries, nothing without a stall); queue.mjs stall-presence; go-loop.sh stall_wait polls person-at-mac.sh idle every 20s during a signin/spend backoff, notifies via notify_person ... return ('Stopped 20h ago while you were away. Sign-in needed...'), logs 'notified you on your return', records stall_notified on=return, and cuts the rest of the wait to 120s so a sign-in is picked up quickly. Dashboard stall hero says when the last notice went out and whether the Mac is idle. Verified: queue/bin/stall-return-drill.sh 13/13 (and all fail with PHOTONZ_STALL_AWAY=999999 as a mutation check), failure-drill.sh all 8 scenarios pass (now with a stand-in idle clock so a real return mid-drill cannot add a notice), manager-due-drill 14/14, Scripts/test.sh green (10985 tests). No app code touched, so no walks and no audit (loop infrastructure only).

A loop stalled on sign-in or the spend limit now notifies the person the first time they return to the Mac after 15 min idle (one per return, none after the stall clears), and cuts its wait to 2 min so their sign-in is picked up quickly. Shipped in go-loop.sh stall_wait, queue-lib advancePresence, queue.mjs stall-presence, dashboard stall hero; loop.log and history (stall_notified on=return) record it. Verified by queue/bin/stall-return-drill.sh (13/13, mutation-checked), failure-drill.sh (all 8), manager-due-drill, Scripts/test.sh green. Commit 264e862e.
